title: Pastor Richard Garcia GUILTY in $6M Church Investment Fraud
summary:
Arlington pastor Richard Garcia, church flipping fraud: on November 19, 2026, a federal jury in Fort Worth found Richard Reinaldo Garcia, 53, guilty of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and three counts of wire fraud. Prosecutors say that from 2021 to 2025 he sold investors "church flipping" deals and Christian concert ventures, had them label payments as "donations" to Gracia Church, and used the money for other expenses. More than 70 victims in the U.S., Colombia, Mexico and the Dominican Republic lost more than $6 million, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office. Sentencing is set for March 4, 2027.
Richard Garcia, Arlington pastor, Gracia Church, Ministerio Gracia, church flipping, pastor fraud, wire fraud, Fort Worth federal court, investment fraud.
The photo of Richard Garcia is part of a government trial exhibit released by the U.S. Attorney's Office (N.D. Tex.).

question: Three churches the government's chart says were never purchased, more than $6 million lost, and what the U.S. Attorney called "a very quick decision by the jury." What sentence should he get? Tell us in the comments.
first_comment: Prosecutors say investors were told to call their money "donations" to the church. Would that have made you suspicious — or made you trust it more?
